product_impacts.description: Disk II is the established same-host disk alternative; retaining Apple disk software can reduce migration work, while FlexiDisk II needs its recorded Apple interface and format qualification.
The Logix card includes a Disk II-compatible controller path as well as FlexiBUS, so the installed Disk II ecosystem can complement the card as well as compete with a new external drive.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare an Apple II with working Disk II software against the 1979 Logix card and qualified FlexiDisk II configuration.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: Disk II uses an Apple controller/disk interface rather than FlexiBUS; disk-format compatibility alone does not convert the transport.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: Existing disks and applications create a switching hurdle. Retaining a qualified Disk II path can make incremental FlexiBUS adoption more attractive; no sales uplift is measured.

product_impacts.description: For an Apple II buyer needing the function this adapter actually supplies, the established native attachment can avoid a FlexiBUS purchase. The Logix card instead provides two FlexiBUS ports and a Disk II path; it does not transparently replace every native adapter.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare alternative Apple II peripheral attachment choices available by the end of 1979; retain native 6502 drivers and required cabling.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: The board retains its native peripheral signalling and software; only functions actually supplied by both purchase paths overlap. Neither the connector nor an adapter implies FlexiBUS device discovery or class compatibility.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: Working native attachments can reduce immediate demand for a new bus. Cross-host reuse could favour FlexiBUS only where the actual device class and host driver are qualified.

product_impacts.description: A self-contained serial terminal can provide an S-100 computer’s console without an internal Logix video card and digital monitor.
The terminal includes its own keyboard. It competes as part of an alternative complete console, not as an electrically interchangeable keyboard.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Use a separately implemented terminal profile on an otherwise supported host; assess the terminal’s actual keys, attributes and control sequences.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: Serial characters and escape sequences do not automatically preserve distinct modifier, selection, function-key or clipboard semantics. Native TUI assignments remain separate from terminal control codes.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: A qualified constrained profile could broaden access to TUI applications, but an unchanged terminal is not compliant. Missing key events and screen features can reduce usability; no universal terminal support is claimed.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare complete console configurations on a host supporting both purchase paths.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: The terminal contains its own display controller and communicates through a serial interface instead of the Logix monitor link.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: It supplies a mature alternative console and may reduce demand for a Logix card/monitor pair. This is competition between complete configurations, not a digital-link compatibility claim.

product_impacts.description: A working native disk controller provides an alternative to buying a FlexiBUS host card for storage; both paths require host-specific qualification.
On a suitably configured S-100 host, native disk storage is a competing purchase path. Capacity, boot support and disk formats must be compared separately; a controller alone is not a complete drive.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare complete usable S-100 disk configurations, including the drive, controller, boot path and operating-system driver.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: Native controller registers and disk timing differ from FlexiBUS sector messages. Existing CP/M disk formats do not establish host-bus or media interchangeability.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: Installed disks and BIOS support can hold users to native controllers. FlexiBUS offers a conditional cross-host reuse argument, subject to throughput and recovery qualification rather than assumed superiority.

standards_impacts.outcomes_description: A working conventional display reduces the need to buy a new monitor/controller pair. Logix must demonstrate benefits in the qualified mode; later professional graphics and 1982 palette extensions are excluded.

product_impacts.description: Conventional I/O ports preserve access to existing serial/parallel equipment. They compete with a FlexiBUS host card only for overlapping peripheral functions; isolated or cassette I/O is not supplied by the Logix card.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare a named qualified S-100 host with its existing peripheral software against the two-port Logix expansion option.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: Register-level serial/parallel I/O does not provide FlexiBUS discovery, framing or class commands. Physical I/O counts are not equivalent to supported device classes.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: Legacy peripherals can make conventional ports preferable in the short term. FlexiBUS adoption depends on useful supported devices and reliable drivers, not on claiming that every old port can be replaced.

On a suitably configured S-100 host, native disk storage is a competing purchase path. Capacity, boot support and disk formats must be compared separately; a controller alone is not a complete drive.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare complete usable S-100 disk configurations, including the drive, controller, boot path and operating-system driver.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: Native controller registers and disk timing differ from FlexiBUS sector messages. Existing CP/M disk formats do not establish host-bus or media interchangeability.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: Installed disks and BIOS support can hold users to native controllers. FlexiBUS offers a conditional cross-host reuse argument, subject to throughput and recovery qualification rather than assumed superiority.

product_impacts.description: Conventional I/O ports preserve access to existing serial/parallel equipment. They compete with a FlexiBUS host card only for overlapping peripheral functions; isolated or cassette I/O is not supplied by the Logix card.

standards_impacts.outcomes_description: Legacy peripherals can make conventional ports preferable in the short term. FlexiBUS adoption depends on useful supported devices and reliable drivers, not on claiming that every old port can be replaced.

product_impacts.description: A self-contained serial terminal can provide an S-100 computer’s console without an internal Logix video card and digital monitor.
The terminal includes its own keyboard. It competes as part of an alternative complete console, not as an electrically interchangeable keyboard.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Use a separately implemented terminal profile on an otherwise supported host; assess the terminal’s actual keys, attributes and control sequences.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: Serial characters and escape sequences do not automatically preserve distinct modifier, selection, function-key or clipboard semantics. Native TUI assignments remain separate from terminal control codes.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: A qualified constrained profile could broaden access to TUI applications, but an unchanged terminal is not compliant. Missing key events and screen features can reduce usability; no universal terminal support is claimed.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare complete console configurations on a host supporting both purchase paths.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: The terminal contains its own display controller and communicates through a serial interface instead of the Logix monitor link.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: It supplies a mature alternative console and may reduce demand for a Logix card/monitor pair. This is competition between complete configurations, not a digital-link compatibility claim.

product_impacts.description: A self-contained serial terminal can provide an S-100 computer’s console without an internal Logix video card and digital monitor.
The terminal includes its own keyboard. It competes as part of an alternative complete console, not as an electrically interchangeable keyboard.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Use a separately implemented terminal profile on an otherwise supported host; assess the terminal’s actual keys, attributes and control sequences.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: Serial characters and escape sequences do not automatically preserve distinct modifier, selection, function-key or clipboard semantics. Native TUI assignments remain separate from terminal control codes.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: A qualified constrained profile could broaden access to TUI applications, but an unchanged terminal is not compliant. Missing key events and screen features can reduce usability; no universal terminal support is claimed.

standards_impacts.assumption_description: Compare complete console configurations on a host supporting both purchase paths.
standards_impacts.comparison_description: The terminal contains its own display controller and communicates through a serial interface instead of the Logix monitor link.
standards_impacts.outcomes_description: It supplies a mature alternative console and may reduce demand for a Logix card/monitor pair. This is competition between complete configurations, not a digital-link compatibility claim.
